html:
The Sultanate of Zanzibar was a state of Omani Arab sultans based on the island of Zanzibar, off the coast of what is now Tanzania, from 1856 to 1964. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900, together with its claims on the mainland coast.

Sultan Said bin Sultan of Muscat and Oman moved his court to Zanzibar around 1840 and filled the island with clove plantations worked by slaves. When he died in 1856, his sons split his realm, and one became sultan of Zanzibar. The island was the great market of the East African slave and ivory trade, fed by caravans led by men such as Tippu Tip.

Under British pressure, Sultan Barghash closed the slave market in 1873. In the 1880s Germany and Britain took the mainland coast, and Zanzibar became a British protectorate in 1890. The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 lasted under an hour. Independence came in 1963. A month later the Zanzibar Revolution overthrew the sultan, and the island joined Tanganyika to form Tanzania.
